extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in international affairs and current events (Cold War-era diplomacy, European politics)
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting of Foreign Ministers' Council deliberations and related international developments (Germany settlement, Marshall Plan debate, Soviet/Western disputes, plus concurrent economic and labor news).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional central German government must reflect free will
rubrics_metrics.description: “This government should reflect the free will of the German people and should be permitted to administer Germany without outside interference except for such necessary security measures as the Allies may jointly decide to impose.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marshall emphasized that a central German government must be real and not a facade; it must reflect Germans' free will and be allowed to administer without outside interference except jointly-decided security measures. Establishing a government alone, without the requisite conditions, would be a sham.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political organization conditional on prior economic unity
rubrics_metrics.description: At Moscow all four delegations formally agreed that: 'any decision on the political organization of Germany is conditional upon the prior establishment of German economic unity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marshall repeated that no German government can function unless the basic essentials on which German economic unity depends are agreed upon and implemented by all four powers and effective guarantees exist for safeguarding fundamental freedoms in all parts of Germany.

rubrics_metrics.name: Basic principles required to enable a German government to function
rubrics_metrics.description: Marshall listed essentials: 'the basic freedom for the individual; the abolition of zonal boundaries, except as delimitation of occupation areas, with no hindrance to the free flow of persons, ideas and goods throughout the whole [of Germany]; and a clear determination of the economic burdens the German people are to bear.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These principles were presented as prerequisites that must be established before a central government can be effective; Marshall urged dropping generalities and acting on these substantive matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Establishment of central German economic agencies
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision was made for the establishment of central German agencies 'which were intended to carry out the economic unity of Germany' and to which three powers had subscribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marshall and others described creation of such agencies as a preliminary step toward establishing a functioning German government; economic agencies implementing unity are practical prerequisites for political unification.

rubrics_metrics.name: United States: favor establishment of provisional government only with conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: The United States 'favors the establishment of a provisional government at the earliest possible moment, but we regard it as dangerous to the security of the Allied nations and to the peace of the world... to pretend that mere setting up of a central German government would result in healing the division of Germany.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: US position balances support for early provisional government with a warning that doing so without agreed economic unity and safeguards would be misleading and dangerous; timing is contingent on prior conditions being met.

rubrics_metrics.name: France's condition for accepting whole Germany as single economic unit
rubrics_metrics.description: France 'has no objection to the whole of Germany being treated as a single economic unit ... without prejudicing the status of the Ruhr and the Rhineland,' provided 'the Saar Valley is integrated into the French economic system.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidault's statement sets a national precondition: France will accept economic unity only if the Saar is integrated into France's economic arrangements while preserving Ruhr/Rhineland status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allied control of the Ruhr (French demand)
rubrics_metrics.description: Bidault listed Allied control of the steel-producing, coal-rich Ruhr—the industrial center of Germany—as one of principal Allied considerations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Control of key industrial regions was presented as a concrete Allied measure to manage German economic capabilities as part of any settlement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Soviet reparations demand (Molotov's asserted condition)
rubrics_metrics.description: Molotov's remarks were interpreted as asserting that Germany must accept a burden of $10,000,000,000 in reparations to Soviet Russia in addition to other conditions for political and economic unification.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marshall asked Molotov to clarify specifically how he proposed the German people meet such an obligation, highlighting reparations as a proposed Soviet precondition that affects negotiation feasibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Security measures to be jointly decided by Allies
rubrics_metrics.description: Any outside interference with a German government would be limited 'except for such necessary security measures as the Allies may jointly decide to impose.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Security arrangements are permissible but must be jointly determined by the occupying powers; such measures are treated as limited exceptions to non-interference in administration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of force guideline for French interior minister: police may use firearms when attacked
rubrics_metrics.description: Interior Minister Jules Moch announced the police 'can use their firearms' if they are being subjected to attacks and have no other means of defending the terrain they occupy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Directive was given amid violent strikes: police authorized to use lethal force only in situations of attack where no other means exist; issued as a rule for restoring order in face of violent unrest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strike conduct directive (orders to strikers)
rubrics_metrics.description: An order purportedly displayed (Communist-related) urged attackers to 'Preserve all stocks of armament material. Do not carry firearms. Use only pick handles, monkey wrenches, stabbing awls and other toothed tools.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This internal strike directive sought to limit visible firearms while encouraging use of improvised weapons and to control handling of armament stocks; presented in account of strike tactics and street violence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for resuming British drawings on U.S. loan
rubrics_metrics.description: The release of the remaining $400,000,000 of Britain's American loan was authorized under an understanding that Britain need not adhere strictly to certain terms of the original loan agreement; the suspension of the dollar-payment clause would enable Britain 'to continue purchases in the United States necessary to maintain its present austerity program' without adding inflationary pressures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treasury and British officials framed the loan resumption as contingent on using funds to support austerity objectives and on arrangements that would avoid adding inflationary pressure; practical economic-policy conditions guided the decision.
